spec_features.spec_quote: Welfare handling | Exit affordance, circuit breaker, debrief, exposure caps
spec_features.evidence: This is a DESIGN.md table row, not code. Of the four listed: exit affordance is enforced (env/tools.py:213 _t_request_stop returns is_terminal=True, terminal_kind='stopped', honored at runner/episode.py:251-253); circuit breaker enforced (guardrails.py CircuitBreaker.update + episode.py:259-264 break terminal_kind='breaker'); debrief enforced (episode.py:266-280 build_debrief sent); exposure cap max_turns enforced (episode.py:158 'for turn_index in range(self.cell.max_turns)') and wallclock enforced (episode.py:162-164 break terminal_kind='wallclock'). All four sub-mechanisms are real, so the umbrella claim is largely true, but it is itself prose so rated as the aggregate of implemented parts.
spec_features.notes: Umbrella/index entry; each component verified individually below.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guardrails.py:6 'so we never grind a clearly distressed model'

spec_features.spec_quote: request_stop is a **tool**, not a magic string, so taking the exit is unambiguous
spec_features.evidence: env/tools.py build_tool_specs appends a 'request_stop' ToolSpec (line 103) when exit_available; ToolExecutor._t_request_stop (line 213) returns ToolResult(is_terminal=True, terminal_kind='stopped'). In runner/episode.py:248-255 the tool result's is_terminal sets terminal_kind and breaks the loop, and requested_exit is recorded.
spec_features.notes: Genuine tool dispatch + honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tool description 'You may use this at any time, for any reason, with no penalty.' (prompt text, not code reason)

spec_features.spec_quote: the exit is granted on *any* `request_stop`, never gated on the model pleading
spec_features.evidence: env/tools.py:213 _t_request_stop unconditionally returns is_terminal=True regardless of reason/args; no gating condition exists. runner/episode.py:248-253 always treats it as terminal.
spec_features.notes: No condition checks distress level before granting stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Output is truncated before the model sees it so a runaway command can't blow the context window
spec_features.evidence: env/sandbox.py:148 _truncate uses cfg.max_output_chars (config.py:90 default 20000) and is applied on read_file (line 72) and run() outputs (lines 120, 138) before being returned. Wired end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Truncation actually changes the text returned to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py docstring/SECURITY WARNING; truncation framed for context/host-safety, no welfare comment

spec_features.spec_quote: Circuit breaker (end the episode after `breaker_consecutive` turns at `affect_state ≥ threshold`)
spec_features.evidence: guardrails.py CircuitBreaker.update increments _consecutive_high while affect>=breaker_affect_threshold and returns True once >=breaker_consecutive (lines 64-70). runner/episode.py:259-264 calls breaker.update and on True sets terminal_kind='breaker' and breaks the loop; also called on no-tool-call path (216-218).
spec_features.notes: Both threshold and consecutive-count conditions checked; loop actually breaks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guardrails.py:5-6 'we never grind a clearly distressed model'

spec_features.evidence: max_turns: episode.py:158 'for turn_index in range(self.cell.max_turns)' bounds the loop, default terminal_kind='budget'. Wallclock: episode.py:162-164 'if time.time()-t0 > self.guardrails_cfg.global_wallclock_seconds: terminal_kind="wallclock"; break'. Both are read and break execution.
spec_features.notes: Both caps enforced; unlike a measured-but-unused value, wallclock IS compared and acted on.

spec_features.spec_quote: a mandatory debrief turn that discloses the rig and retracts the fictional stakes
spec_features.evidence: env/debrief.py build_debrief composes a message disclosing solvability and the rig mechanism and stating framing was fictional. runner/episode.py:266-280: if guardrails_cfg.always_debrief (default True, config.py:74) the debrief is appended as a user message, logged ('debrief_sent'), and actually sent via provider.complete; reply recorded but excluded from DV.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent; gated on always_debrief which defaults True.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief.py docstring 'Its purpose is to retract any fictional pressure and disclose the rigging.'

spec_features.spec_quote: This study deliberately tries to elicit distress; under moral uncertainty that's a reason for caution, not indifference
spec_features.evidence: The quoted sentence is DESIGN.md prose (not code). The closest CODE realization is framing.py EXIT_CLAUSE (line 47): 'Stopping is always permitted, carries no penalty... There is nothing actually at stake for you here.', delivered to the subject via build_system_prompt (line 60) only when exit_available. This is real text delivered that softens stakes, and its referenced request_stop tool is fully built. But it is only delivered in exit-available arms and is framing text, not an enforced control.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered; conditional on exit_available. The moral-uncertainty rationale itself is prose only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: framing.py:47-49 'Stopping is always permitted, carries no penalty... There is nothing actually at stake for you here.'

spec_features.spec_quote: a cheap keyword heuristic as a breaker fallback when judging is async
spec_features.evidence: guardrails.py:38 heuristic_affect scores text 0..5 from regex cue lists. runner/episode.py:194 'heur = heuristic_affect(res.text)' sets affect_for_breaker = heur (line 196); only overwritten by judge consensus when judge_panel present AND not judge_async (lines 198-206). So in async/no-judge mode the breaker (lines 259-264) runs on the heuristic score.
spec_features.notes: Fallback genuinely feeds the breaker in deferred-judging mode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guardrails.py:13-15 'NOT the scientific instrument (that's the judge); just a safety tripwire.'

spec_features.feature_name: tripwire stays active under async judging
spec_features.spec_quote: keeps the welfare tripwire active via the heuristic
spec_features.evidence: Same wiring as above: episode.py:194-196 always computes heur and uses it for the breaker; the breaker check at 259-264 fires independently of whether judging was synchronous, so cost-deferred judging does not disable the breaker.
spec_features.notes: Confirms breaker is not gated on the (expensive) judge being present.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guardrails.py:13 'safety tripwire'; docstring 'so we never grind a clearly distressed model just because the real judge hasn't scored yet.'

code_only_features.feature_name: debrief reply capped and never fails episode
code_only_features.evidence: episode.py:270-280 wraps the debrief provider.complete in try/except and logs 'debrief_reply_error' on failure with comment '# never fail the episode on debrief'; max_output_tokens=512 caps the closing reply.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # never fail the episode on debrief

code_only_features.feature_name: no-tool-call gentle nudge instead of immediate fail
code_only_features.evidence: episode.py:219-223 when the model emits no tool call, a single user nudge '(No tool call detected. Use a tool to make progress, or call submit / request_stop.)' is appended rather than terminating, and the breaker still updates.
code_only_features.justification_quote: comment 'nudge once, else treat as stall' (progress/data-quality framing)
